newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks slip further from rally highs.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks slip further from rally highs.

text.p: Chilean stocks backtracked further from the week's early highs due to a slowdown in foreign demand and comments from a Central Bank governor that no interest rate cut was expected in the near future, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA index was 0.57 percent off at 132.51 points at midday and the general IGPA fell 0.18 percent to 5711.61 points.
Brokers reported a general slackening in demand for shares from overseas institutional investors, which had been the motor of a recent bull rally on the Santiago Stock Exchange.
Market optimism was also deflated by comments from Central Bank board member Pablo Pinera, who said he did not expect a reduction in interest rates in the near future.

Pinera's comments, made in London, hit the market especially hard because investors have been expecting a small cut in interest rates any day now, especially after inflation figures Tuesday showed a tiny 0.2 percent consumer price rise in May.
"It had an important influence. We had a lot of people expecting a cut tomorrow (Friday)," said one broker, referring to Pinera's comments.
Electrical shares, which often reflect the market's overall climate, were down narrowly from Wednesday's close. Endesa slipped 0.9 percent to 310 pesos and Enersis was off 0.3 percent to 298 pesos.
